newsitem.title: USA: Bond dealers ask US tax panel for help on veto law.
newsitem.headline: Bond dealers ask US tax panel for help on veto law.

text.p: Bond dealers on Monday asked a key U.S. congressional panel to clarify how the new line- item veto law signed by President Clinton in April would apply in the tax-exempt bond market.
The bill, which takes effect in January 1997, allows the president to cancel any revenue-losing tax provision that gives a tax preference to 100 or fewer beneficiaries.

PSA, the Bond Market Trade Association, said in a two-page letter to the Joint Committee on Taxation on December 13, that there is a "great deal of uncertainty" about how the provision applies to tax-exempt bonds.
The assocation released a copy of the letter on Monday.

PSA said it is particularly concerned about how the law's "aggregation rule" would affect tax-exempts. That provision says that "all holders of the same bond issue should be treated (as) a single beneficiary."
PSA said a recent analysis of the bill prepared by the joint committee needs to clarify whether or not issuers and their obligors on bond issues would be covered separately.

"In many cases, issuers issue tax-exempt bonds on behalf of a number of obligors. We believe that treating each obligor as a beneficiary would be consistent with the underlying principle of the Act," says the letter, signed by PSA Executive Vice President Micah Green.
Green's letter was addressed to Kenneth Kies, chief of staff of the joint committee.
